quick: IR 50-100 mg q4-6h; ER 50 mg q12h
Avoid ER in severe impairment; caution IR
Reduce dose; avoid in severe impairment
Respiration, sedation, pain, abuse, bowel function
summary: Tapentadol is a centrally acting analgesic combining mu-opioid receptor agonism with norepinephrine reuptake inhibition, used for moderate-to-severe acute pain (immediate-release) and severe chronic/neuropathic (diabetic) pain (extended-release). Habit forming: Yes - it is a controlled opioid. Boxed warnings cover addiction/abuse/misuse, life-threatening respiratory depression, neonatal opioid withdrawal, and fatal interaction with benzodiazepines/CNS depressants. Contraindicated with MAOIs.
indications: Management of moderate to severe acute pain in adults (immediate-release)
Management of severe, persistent pain requiring daily long-term opioid therapy when alternatives are inadequate (extended-release)
Severe neuropathic pain of diabetic peripheral neuropathy in adults (extended-release)

dosage.n: Day 1 a second dose may be given after 1 h; max 700 mg day 1, 600 mg/day thereafter
Titrate by 50 mg/dose every 3 days as needed

dosage.d: IR 50 mg no more often than q8h (max 3 doses/day); ER 50 mg once daily

admin: Immediate-release: swallow tablets whole or as directed; with or without food
Extended-release: swallow whole - never crush, chew, split or dissolve (risk of fatal rapid release)
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Do not abruptly discontinue in physically dependent patients - taper gradually
Avoid all other CNS depressants and alcohol; assess abuse risk before and during therapy
moa: Tapentadol is a dual-mechanism analgesic: it is an agonist at mu-opioid receptors and inhibits neuronal reuptake of norepinephrine, enhancing descending inhibitory pain pathways. The combined action provides analgesia for nociceptive and neuropathic pain with somewhat less opioid-mediated gastrointestinal effect than pure mu-agonists.

absolute: Acute or severe bronchial asthma/hypercarbia in unmonitored setting
Known or suspected GI obstruction including paralytic ileus
Concurrent MAOI use or within 14 days
relative: Elderly, debilitated, or significant pulmonary disease

preg: Prolonged use in pregnancy can cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening. Use only if benefit justifies risk and monitor the neonate closely; avoid where possible.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding due to potential for serious adverse effects (sedation, respiratory depression) in the infant.
renal: Not studied in severe renal impairment - the extended-release form is not recommended; use immediate-release with caution. No adjustment needed in mild-to-moderate impairment.
hepatic: Reduce dose in moderate hepatic impairment (IR 50 mg up to every 8 hours; ER 50 mg once daily). Avoid in severe hepatic impairment.

major: MAOIs - contraindicated; risk of serotonin syndrome/hypertensive crisis
Benzodiazepines and other CNS depressants - profound sedation, respiratory depression, death
Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans) - serotonin syndrome
moderate: Other opioids and mixed agonist/antagonists - may precipitate withdrawal or reduce analgesia
Anticholinergics - increased risk of urinary retention/constipation
Diuretics - reduced efficacy via ADH release
minor: Strong enzyme inducers - may lower tapentadol exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Contraindicated/avoid - additive CNS and respiratory depression can be fatal, and accelerates ER drug release.
interactions.diagnostics: May interfere with some urine opioid immunoassays.

monitoring: Respiratory rate, oxygenation and level of sedation, especially on initiation/titration
Signs of opioid misuse, addiction or diversion
Bowel function (prophylactic laxatives) and signs of serotonin syndrome
counsel: This medicine is habit forming - take exactly as prescribed and do not share it
Never crush or chew extended-release tablets and do not drink alcohol
Seek emergency help for very slow/shallow breathing or extreme drowsiness; keep naloxone available
Do not stop suddenly after regular use - it must be tapered
Avoid driving until you know how it affects you and tell your doctor about all other medicines
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep secured from misuse
pearls: Habit forming opioid (Schedule II) - boxed warnings for addiction, respiratory depression, neonatal withdrawal and CNS-depressant interaction
Dual mu-agonist + norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor - useful for neuropathic pain
Contraindicated with MAOIs and high serotonin-syndrome risk with serotonergic drugs
Naloxone reverses opioid effect - have it available for at-risk patients
Lower opioid-type GI side effects than morphine but still causes constipation
missed: For scheduled (ER) dosing, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is near the next dose, then skip it - never double up. For PRN immediate-release use, only take when pain requires it and respect the minimum interval.
overdose: Overdose causes respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils, somnolence progressing to stupor/coma, hypotension and possibly seizures. Give naloxone, secure the airway, support ventilation and circulation, and monitor closely (repeat naloxone may be needed for ER formulations due to prolonged release).
